meta.method: per-exposure fixed-position PSF photometry (pixel-integrated Gaussian, FWHM = PSF_FWHM of the exposure) fitting the target together with the known neighbours within 25 arcsec, so their light is removed; total flux, no aperture correction; flagged = non-informational FLAGS bit within 1.5 px; saturated = early overflow (OVERFLOW+SUR_ERROR) or NONLINEAR within 2 px (flux = lower limit; such exposures fall back to aperture photometry, point.photometry = 'aperture'); overflow = recovered overflow pixels (valid; recovered/clean median 1.04, 10 pairs, range 1.00-1.51); neighbor_flux = fitted flux of the removed neighbours. Systematic: the Gaussian PSF leaves ~5-15% of a neighbour's flux as a residual on the target (measured on WISE 0855 / G=16.3 star at 3-11 arcsec), so treat |flux| < 0.15 x neighbor_flux as consistent with zero
